title: Model Change Approval & Customer Governance Runbook
author: Marcos Rivera
content:
Summary
-------
This runbook defines the governance, approval paths, operational checks, and customer communication templates for any model or model-configuration change that impacts enterprise customers (Hosted, Dedicated, or Private deployments). It is intended for Customer Success, Product, SRE, Serving Runtime, and Security teams. The goal is to reduce surprise regressions, keep customers informed, and make rollbacks predictable.

Scope
-----
- Applies to model version swaps, quantization profile changes, prompt-template migrations, model serving config changes (e.g., max_tokens, sampling defaults), and runtime kernel changes that may alter output semantics or latency by >5%.
- Includes both Redwood-initiated and customer-requested changes for enterprise tenants.
- Excludes purely infra-only upgrades that do not alter model observable behavior (see Appendix A for classification rules).

Why we need this
-----------------
Enterprise customers require predictable output quality and clear change windows. Uncoordinated changes generate escalations, churn risk, and operational burden. This runbook balances speed with customer safety using a two-track approval model (minor vs major) and objective telemetry gates.

Primary stakeholders and ownership
---------------------------------
- Customer Success (CS): final customer communications, risk assessment for accounts, QBR notes.
- Product: change justification, rollout strategy, canary criteria.
- Eng - Serving Runtime: technical rollout, canary execution, rollback hooks.
- Eng - SRE: capacity and latency SLO guardrails, escalation path.
- Security/Compliance: signoff for private deployments or regulated customers.
- Owner: Customer Success (contact: marcos.rivera@redwood.com).

Decision categories (classification)
-----------------------------------
1) Minor change (fast-track):
   - Non-production-facing prompt-template tweaks, minor sampling seed updates, telemetry-only instrumentation.
   - Expected impact: negligible change to model outputs; latency delta <5%.
   - Approval: Product + CS peer review.
2) Major change (full review):
   - Model family change (e.g., v1->v2), quantization profile change altering float->int path, new architecture variant, or changes that affect factuality/behavior.
   - Expected impact: potential behavioral regressions or latency change >=5%.
   - Approval: Product + CS + Serving Runtime + SRE + Security (if Private) + Exec sponsor.

Approval matrix (summary)
-------------------------
- Minor: Product (owner) -> CS notify -> rollout during maintenance window or low-traffic canary.
- Major: Model Change Request (MCR) RFC -> Cross-functional review meeting -> Signed approval via ticket (Jira PRD) -> Scheduled canary -> Customer opt-in for early testing or staged opt-out.

Pre-change checklist (must be completed before any scheduled rollout)
-------------------------------------------------------------------
- Define classification (minor/major) and document justification.
- Owner assigns cross-functional reviewers (list in ticket).
- Identify impacted customers (list enterprise tenants) and their SLA tier.
- Create a rollback plan with RTO goals and quick rollback triggers.
- Create automated telemetry assertions (see Telemetry & validations).
- Schedule rollout window and reserve SRE on-call for the change window + 2 hours.
- Draft customer-facing communication (CS drafts, Product approves).

Change execution procedure (canary & rollout)
-------------------------------------------
1) Pre-canary steps (T-48 to T-2 hours):
   - Deploy change to internal staging and run the predefined prompt-suite (see Appendix B).
   - Run synthetic traffic at production-like token distribution for 30m.
   - Verify cost delta and latency distribution vs baseline.
2) Canary (T):
   - Route 0.5-2% steady-state traffic from canary tenants or synthetic tenancy to the new variant for 1 hour.
   - Run automated evals: output-delta metric, hallucination score, top-k token distribution, and latency P95.
   - Monitor errors and backend resource consumption.
3) Scale canary (T+1h):
   - If all assertions pass, increase to 10% for 2 hours.
   - If still green, schedule a rolling increase with checkpoints at 25%, 50%, 100% each with 2-hour observation windows.
4) Abort/rollback:
   - Any assertion failure or customer-reported regression escalates to the Runbook Owner who initiates rollback. See Rollback criteria.

Telemetry & validations (objective gates)
---------------------------------------
Create assertions that are executed automatically during rollout. Example set: 
- Functional quality: output-delta rate < 2% across canonical prompt-set (per tenant).
- Hallucination signal: composite hallucination score delta <= 0.5 points (normalized).
- Latency: P95 latency delta <= 15% absolute or <= 200ms (whichever is smaller).
- Error budget: 5xx rate not to exceed 0.1% above baseline.
- Cost: per-token compute cost delta <= 10% for Dedicated customers without prior consent.
- Tokenization/regression checks: no >0.2% increase in truncation/invalid-token counts.

Incident/escalation flow for regressions during rollout
-----------------------------------------------------
1) Tier 1 detection: automated assertion breach -> Alert on Slack #canary-alerts and PagerDuty to Serving Runtime on-call.
2) Triage (10–30 minutes): Owner and runtime on-call validate and reproduce.
3) Customer notification (30–60 minutes): If customer MCR was not pre-signed, CS sends a status update using the "Short Incident Notice" template below.
4) Decision window (60–120 minutes): Either quick rollback or targeted mitigation (e.g., revert sampling param).
5) Postmortem and RCA: If rollback occurred or customer impact exceeded 15 minutes, open a postmortem ticket and schedule a cross-team review in 3 business days.

Rollback criteria (explicit triggers)
-----------------------------------
- Any assertion breach listed above for >15 minutes sustained.
- More than one enterprise tenant reports a reproducible semantic regression within 60 minutes.
- P95 latency increase >250ms causing SLA violation risk.
- Unexpected 5xx spike >0.5% absolute.
- Cost surge alarm for Dedicated customer where budget controls exist.

Customer communication templates (use and adapt per account)
-----------------------------------------------------------
1) Short Incident Notice (for initial outreach):
Subject: Service update: model rollout observation - [CustomerName]
Body:
Hi [CustomerName] team,
We are observing an unexpected behavior during a model update that may impact a subset of requests. We have paused the rollout for your tenant and our engineering team is investigating. We will share an update within 60 minutes and provide mitigation steps if needed.
Best,
[CS Rep]

2) Post-Rollback Summary (within 24 hours):
Subject: Post-rollback summary & next steps - [CustomerName]
Body:
Hi [CustomerName],
We reverted the recent model change for your tenant at [time]. Summary of what happened, impact window, and next steps (including optional test schedule and QBR notes). Attach the synthetic test-report PDF and link to the RCA when available.

Post-change QA and QBR integration
----------------------------------
- Add the change event to the next customer QBR agenda under "Operational Changes & Risk" with: description, canary metrics, customer impact (if any), and recommended next steps.
- Maintain a change log for each enterprise tenant with: change id, date, owner, pre/post metric snapshots, and artifacts (test reports, canary dashboards).

Edge cases and private deployments
---------------------------------
- For Private deployments, Security must confirm that the new model binary/quantization artifacts meet the customer FIPS/HSM constraints before approval.
- For heavily regulated customers (marked in account metadata as "regulated: true"), require an explicit customer opt-in unless the change is security-critical.

Operational tooling and runbook automation
----------------------------------------
- Use the MCR (Model Change Request) ticket template in Jira and attach: rationale, canary plan, telemetry assertions, rollback plan, impacted tenant list, and customer comms draft.
- Canary dashboards: link to Grafana panels: model_canary_{change_id}_quality and model_canary_{change_id}_latency.
- Automate assertion evaluation via the canary-orchestrator job (CLI example below).

CLI examples and request payloads
--------------------------------
- Start a canary run (internal):
  redwood-canaryctl start --change-id MCR-1234 --duration 60m --traffic 2% --prompt-suite default-sanity

- Example MCR JSON payload (attach to Jira):
  {
    "change_id": "MCR-1234",
    "author": "marcos.rivera@redwood.com",
    "classification": "major",
    "description": "Upgrade from model-x-1.3 to model-x-2.0 (chiefly factuality and perf improvements)",
    "impact_scope": ["tenant-abc", "tenant-xyz"],
    "telemetry_assertions": ["output-delta<2%","p95-latency-delta<15%"],
    "rollback_plan": "automated switch to model-x-1.3 and invalidate kvcache for canary tenants",
    "scheduled_window": "2026-07-29T02:00:00Z/2026-07-29T06:00:00Z"
  }

Note: The JSON above should be pasted into the Jira change artifact.

Postmortem and RCA expectations
-------------------------------
- If the change causes customer-visible regression, open a postmortem within 24 hours. Include: timeline, root causes, detection signals, and action items with owners and due dates.
- If regression is prevented by telemetry, capture the assertion data and mark the MCR as "near-miss". Add to monthly governance review for trending.

Appendix A — classification decision rules (quick)
------------------------------------------------
- If the change modifies model weights or tokenizer, classify as Major.
- If change only tweaks hyperparameters that do not cross a rational threshold (e.g., temperature 0.7->0.72), classify as Minor.
- If ambiguity remains, default to Major and follow full signoff.

Appendix B — recommended canonical prompt-suite (summary)
---------------------------------------------------------
- Customer-canonical: 30 representative prompts derived from top-ten customer intents.
- Safety-canonical: 40 prompts designed to surface hallucinations, instruction following, and refusal behavior.
- Latency-canonical: 20 long-sequence prompts (avg 1024 tokens).

Appendix C — escalation contacts
-------------------------------
- CS Runbook Owner: marcos.rivera@redwood.com (Pager: paged via #cs-runbook)
- Serving Runtime on-call: runtime-oncall@redwood.com (PagerDuty)
- SRE: sre-oncall@redwood.com
- Security: security-escalation@redwood.com

Revision history
----------------
- 2026-03-11: Created by Marcos Rivera.
- 2026-07-20: Added explicit telemetry assertions and Private deployment signoff requirement.

This document should be used as a normative checklist for all enterprise-impacting model changes. Questions or suggested updates should be submitted to the runbook owner or opened as a Confluence comment against this page.
